source.text: Καὶ ἐλθόντων πρὸς τὸν ὄχλον προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἄνθρωπος γονυπετῶν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐλέησόν μου τὸν υἱόν, ὅτι σεληνιάζεται καὶ κακῶς πάσχει, πολλάκις γὰρ πίπτει εἰς τὸ πῦρ καὶ πολλάκις εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ.

records.literal_gloss: And having come they to the crowd came to him a man kneeling before him \v 15 and saying, Lord, have mercy on of me the son, because he is moonstruck and badly suffers; often for he falls into the fire and often into the water.

en.L: And when they came to the crowd, a man came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, kneeling before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \v 15 and saying, "Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is epileptic and suffers terribly; for often he falls into the fire, and often into the water.
en.B: When they reached the crowd, a man came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and knelt in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 15 "Lord," he said, "take pity on my son. He has seizures and suffers terribly. Time and again he falls into the fire, and time and again into the water.
en.R: Jesus and the three followers came back to the crowd. A man came to Jesus and knelt down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 15 He said, "Lord, please be kind to my son. He has seizures, and he suffers terribly. Many times he falls into the fire or into the water.

decisions.choice: epileptic: having seizures, thought to be moonstruck
decisions.reason: The word means "moonstruck", as in 4:24. People linked seizures with the moon. Falling into fire and water fits the seizures of epilepsy; Matthew also says a demon caused them (17:18).

decisions.choice: kneeling before him: a humble plea
decisions.reason: Kneeling showed respect and earnest request. The man asks for help for his son.

decisions.choice: have mercy: help in pity
decisions.reason: The cry asks Jesus to act out of pity, as in 9:27 and 15:22.

decisions.choice: has seizures (B, R); epileptic (L)
decisions.reason: Literal uses the medical word as in 4:24; Balanced and Readable describe the condition.

decisions.choice: Jesus and the three followers
decisions.reason: Readable says who came down from the mountain.

decisions.choice: es epiléptico (L); tiene ataques (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word pictures the boy as struck by the moon, the old explanation of seizures (meaning decision m1). "Lunático" now means a madman in Spanish, so Literal says "epiléptico" and Balanced and Readable describe the seizures, as the English does.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("dit", 17:20, 17:25)
decisions.reason: As in Mark and Luke: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; the passé composé is how French is spoken and how young readers meet stories, so Readable uses it throughout. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level.

decisions.choice: les disciples at Readable too (for the whole passage)
decisions.reason: English Readable says "followers" because "disciples" is church language in English. French "disciple" is an everyday word for someone who follows a teacher, and Mark and Luke keep it at Readable, so this passage does the same (17:16, 17:19, 17:22-23).

decisions.choice: ana kifafa
decisions.reason: The Greek word pictures the boy as struck by the moon, the old explanation of seizures (meaning decision m1). "Kifafa" is the everyday Swahili word for an illness with seizures, so it serves at every level.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa, xin thương xót" with "tôi" for the father and "cháu" for his son
alternatives: "con" for the father, as the Canaanite woman in 15:22
decisions.reason: He kneels and calls Jesus Lord in a plea for mercy, so he says "Lạy Chúa"; as a grown man and not a disciple he speaks of himself as "tôi", as the officer does in 8:6. A Vietnamese parent speaking to a respected person calls his child "cháu" (Mark 9:17). A reviewer may prefer "con" here as in 15:22.

decisions.choice: "động kinh" at every level
decisions.reason: As in 4:24: the Greek word means "moonstruck", a picture Vietnamese does not have, so every level uses the medical word (meaning decision and footnote).

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 17:14-27; the father speaks to Jesus in 합쇼체 with "주님"
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so respect for Jesus is carried by -시- and 께서 (style guide, sections 4 and 7); kyrie as an address is "주님" in the Korean Matthew.

decisions.choice: "뇌전증" (L); "발작을 일으키다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means "moonstruck", the ancient name for an illness with seizures (meaning decision, with footnote). "뇌전증" is the current Korean name; the older "간질" is now avoided as stigmatizing. Balanced and Readable describe the seizures.

decisions.choice: tem misericórdia (L); tem compaixão (B); tem pena (R)
decisions.reason: The father speaks to Jesus, so the imperative is the "tu" form "tem" at every level (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4), not the "você" form "tenha".

decisions.choice: unbelieving and twisted generation: Deuteronomy 32:5
decisions.reason: In the song of Moses, Israel in the wilderness is called a twisted and crooked generation (Deuteronomy 32:5, 20). Jesus uses the same words of the people of his day.

decisions.choice: you: the people of this generation, the disciples included
alternatives: the father and the crowd only
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to all of them. The disciples are included, since their failure is the occasion (17:16, 20).

decisions.choice: unbelieving: without trust in God
decisions.reason: The word is the opposite of faith. Jesus names the same lack in 17:20.

decisions.choice: faithless (B); unbelieving (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a word that ties the rebuke to "faith" in 17:20.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the people of this generation, the disciples among them (meaning decision m2), so every plural "you" and its verb in verses 17-20 is the reader setting: ustedes forms (the default) or vosotros forms.

decisions.choice: pervertie
decisions.reason: The word means bent out of the right way, and the phrase recalls Deuteronomy 32:5 (m1). "Tordue" is the bare picture but sounds colloquial in French ("an odd, crooked mind"); "pervertie" says a generation turned from what is right, which Readable spells out.

decisions.choice: "các người" for "you"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 9:19: Jesus speaks to the whole generation, the disciples included (meaning decision), so he uses the word for a crowd.

decisions.choice: "thế hệ không tin và gian tà" (L); "vô tín và lệch lạc" (B); "người đời nay ... đi lệch khỏi điều ngay thẳng" (R)
decisions.reason: "Twisted" echoes Deuteronomy 32:5 (meaning decision), a people bent away from what is straight; "thế hệ" (L, B) and "người đời nay" (R) as in 16:4.

decisions.choice: "믿음이 없고 비뚤어진 세대" (L, B); "오늘날 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 9:19, keeping the link with "믿음" in 17:20; "비뚤어진" says "twisted" (Deuteronomy 32:5, meaning decision) in current Korean, where "패역한" is archaic. Readable names the people as the Korean Matthew 12:39 does.

decisions.choice: incrédula e distorcida (L); sem fé e desviada (B)
decisions.reason: The second word means bent out of shape (m1, Deuteronomy 32:5): Literal says "distorcida", Balanced "desviada", turned from the right way. "Perversa" today suggests depravity. Balanced says "sem fé" so the rebuke ties to "fé" in 17:20, as the English "faithless" does.

decisions.choice: bear with: put up with, endure patiently
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold up under something hard. The question is spoken in sorrow as well as rebuke.

decisions.choice: be patient with
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday phrase, as in Mark 9:19.

en.B: Bring the boy over here to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

fr.R: Amenez le garçon ici, près de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »

vi.L: Hãy đem nó đến đây cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.B: Hãy đem đứa bé lại đây cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Hãy đem đứa bé lại đây cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

decisions.choice: bring: a plural command, said to those standing there
decisions.reason: The command is plural. Jesus turns from rebuke to help.

decisions.choice: the boy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the son so the pronoun is not taken for Jesus.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Tráiganme|Traedme}}, with no deity_pronoun span on "me"
decisions.reason: The command is plural, said to those standing there (meaning decision m1), so it takes the plural_you setting; English "bring" shows no number. Spanish joins "me" to the command, so the deity_pronoun setting has no separate word to capitalise.

source.text: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὸ δαιμόνιον· καὶ ἐθεραπεύθη ὁ παῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.

records.literal_gloss: And rebuked it the Jesus, and came out from him the demon; and was healed the boy from the hour that.

en.L: And Jesus rebuked it, and the demon came out of him, and the boy was healed from that hour.
en.B: Jesus spoke sternly to the demon, and it came out of the boy. From that moment he was well.
en.R: Jesus gave a strong command to the demon, and it came out of the boy. Right away the boy was healed.

es.L: Y Jesús lo reprendió, y el demonio salió de él, y el muchacho fue sanado a partir de aquella hora.
es.B: Jesús reprendió con severidad al demonio, y este salió del muchacho. Desde ese momento quedó sano.
es.R: Jesús le dio una orden fuerte al demonio, y el demonio salió del muchacho. En ese mismo momento el muchacho quedó sano.

fr.L: Et Jésus le réprimanda, et le démon sortit de lui, et l’enfant fut guéri dès cette heure-là.
fr.B: Jésus parla sévèrement au démon, et celui-ci sortit de l’enfant. À partir de ce moment, l’enfant fut guéri.
fr.R: Jésus a donné un ordre sévère au démon, et le démon est sorti du garçon. Tout de suite, le garçon a été guéri.

sw.L: Na Yesu akamkemea, na yule pepo akatoka ndani yake, na mvulana akaponywa kuanzia saa hiyo.
sw.B: Yesu alimkemea yule pepo kwa ukali, naye akamtoka mvulana. Tangu wakati huo mvulana alikuwa mzima.
sw.R: Yesu alimpa yule pepo amri kali, naye akamtoka mvulana. Mara moja mvulana akapona.

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu quở nó, và con quỷ ra khỏi đứa bé, và đứa bé được lành từ giờ ấy.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nghiêm khắc ra lệnh cho con quỷ, và nó ra khỏi đứa bé. Ngay từ lúc đó, đứa bé được lành.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nghiêm khắc ra lệnh cho con quỷ, và nó ra khỏi đứa bé. Ngay lập tức đứa bé được chữa lành.

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서 그것을 꾸짖으시자 귀신이 그 아이에게서 나갔다. 그리고 그때부터 아이가 나았다.
ko.B: 예수께서 귀신을 꾸짖으시자, 귀신이 아이에게서 나갔다. 그 순간부터 아이는 나았다.
ko.R: 예수께서 귀신에게 엄하게 명령하셨다. 그러자 귀신이 아이에게서 나갔다. 아이는 바로 그때 나았다.

pt.L: E Jesus o repreendeu, e o demônio saiu dele; e o menino foi curado desde aquela hora.
pt.B: Jesus falou com severidade ao demônio, e ele saiu do menino. Desde aquele momento, o menino ficou bom.
pt.R: Jesus deu uma ordem forte ao demônio, e ele saiu do menino. Na mesma hora, o menino ficou curado.

decisions.choice: rebuked it: Jesus rebuked the demon
decisions.reason: The pronoun could be "him" or "it". The next words say the demon came out, and Mark 9:25 says Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit.

decisions.choice: from that hour: at once, and from then on
decisions.reason: As in 8:13 and 9:22, the healing was immediate and lasting.

decisions.choice: the demon: here the seizures are the work of a demon
alternatives: every illness is caused by demons
decisions.reason: Matthew sometimes tells of illness without demons and sometimes with them (4:24). In this boy's case a demon was at work.

decisions.choice: spoke sternly to (B); gave a strong command to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the rebuke, as in 8:26.

decisions.choice: the demon
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the demon at once.

decisions.choice: demonio
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Spanish: "demonio" at every level for this word, as in Mark 16:9.

decisions.choice: pepo
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Swahili: "pepo" at every level for this word. "Shetani" is kept for Satan himself, as in 16:23.

decisions.choice: "quở" (L); "nghiêm khắc ra lệnh" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:26: "quở" for the Greek "rebuke" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say what Jesus did to the demon.

decisions.choice: "꾸짖다" (L, B), "엄하게 명령하다" (R); "귀신"; "그때부터" (L), "그 순간부터" (B), "바로 그때" (R)
decisions.reason: "Hour" means at once and from then on (meaning decision), as in the Korean Matthew 15:28; "귀신" is the Korean Gospels' word for a demon.

source.text: Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ κατ’ ἰδίαν εἶπον· Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό;

records.literal_gloss: Then having come the disciples to the Jesus privately said, Because of what we not were able to cast out it?

en.L: Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said, "Why were we not able to cast it out?"
en.B: Then, when they were alone with Jesus, the disciples asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What kept us from driving it out?"
en.R: Later the followers came to Jesus when no one else was around. They asked, "Why could we not make the demon leave?"

es.L: Entonces, acercándose los discípulos a Jesús en privado, dijeron: «¿Por qué nosotros no pudimos expulsarlo?».
es.B: Después, cuando estaban a solas con Jesús, los discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Qué nos impidió expulsarlo?».
es.R: Más tarde, los discípulos fueron a ver a Jesús cuando no había nadie más. Le preguntaron: «¿Por qué no pudimos nosotros hacer salir al demonio?».

fr.L: Alors les disciples, s’étant approchés de Jésus en privé, dirent : « Pourquoi n’avons-nous pas pu, nous, le chasser ? »
fr.B: Alors, quand ils furent seuls avec Jésus, les disciples {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demandèrent : « Qu’est-ce qui nous a empêchés de le chasser ? »
fr.R: Plus tard, les disciples sont venus voir Jésus quand il n’y avait personne d’autre. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé : « Pourquoi est-ce que nous n’avons pas pu faire sortir le démon ? »

sw.L: Kisha wanafunzi walimkaribia Yesu walipokuwa peke yao, wakasema, "Kwa sababu gani sisi hatukuweza kumfukuza?"
sw.B: Baadaye, walipokuwa peke yao pamoja na Yesu, wanafunzi walimwuliza, "Ni nini kilichotuzuia sisi kumfukuza?"
sw.R: Baadaye wanafunzi walimwendea Yesu wakati hapakuwa na watu wengine. Wakamwuliza, "Kwa nini sisi hatukuweza kumtoa yule pepo?"

vi.L: Bấy giờ các môn đồ đến riêng với Đức Giê-xu và thưa: "Tại sao chúng con không thể đuổi nó ra được?"
vi.B: Sau đó, khi ở riêng với Đức Giê-xu, các môn đồ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Tại sao chúng con lại không đuổi được nó ra?"
vi.R: Sau đó, khi không có ai khác ở đó, các môn đồ đến hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Tại sao chúng con không đuổi được con quỷ ấy ra?"

ko.L: 그때에 제자들이 따로 예수께 다가와서 말했다. "어찌하여 저희는 그것을 쫓아낼 수 없었습니까?"
ko.B: 그 뒤에 제자들이 따로 예수께 와서 물었다. "왜 저희는 그 귀신을 쫓아내지 못했습니까?"
ko.R: 나중에 다른 사람들이 없을 때 제자들이 예수께 왔다. 그리고 물었다. "왜 저희는 그 귀신을 쫓아내지 못했습니까?"

pt.L: Então os discípulos, aproximando-se de Jesus em particular, disseram: "Por que nós não conseguimos expulsá-lo?"
pt.B: Depois, quando estavam a sós com Jesus, os discípulos {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} perguntaram: "O que nos impediu de expulsá-lo?"
pt.R: Mais tarde, os seguidores foram até Jesus quando não havia mais ninguém por perto. Eles perguntaram: "Por que nós não conseguimos fazer o demônio sair?"

decisions.choice: we: stressed; they had driven out demons before
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out for emphasis. Jesus had sent them out with authority over demons (10:1, 8), so they are puzzled at their failure.

decisions.choice: What kept us from
decisions.reason: Balanced asks the same question in a natural way.

decisions.choice: the demon
decisions.reason: Readable names what they could not drive out.

decisions.choice: "chúng con" for the disciples
decisions.reason: As in Mark 9:28: the disciples speak of themselves as "chúng con" before their teacher.

decisions.choice: "저희는"
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 9:28: the disciples speak humbly to their teacher; the stressed "we" (meaning decision) is carried by the placement of "저희는".

source.text: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τὴν ὀλιγοπιστίαν ὑμῶν· ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως, ἐρεῖτε τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ· Μετάβα ἔνθεν ἐκεῖ, καὶ μεταβήσεται, καὶ οὐδὲν ἀδυνατήσει ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: He and says to them, Because of the little faith of you; truly for I say to you, if you have faith as a seed of mustard, you will say to the mountain this, Move from here to there, and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Because of your little faith. For truly I tell you, if you have faith like a grain of mustard, you will say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you."
en.B: He told them, "It is because your faith is so small. Truly I tell you, if you have faith even the size of a mustard seed, you can tell this mountain, 'Go from here to over there,' and it will go. There will be nothing you cannot do."
en.R: Jesus answered, "It is because you have so little faith. I tell you the truth, suppose your faith is only as big as a tiny mustard seed. Even then you can say to this mountain, 'Move from here to over there,' and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dice: «A causa de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} poca fe. Porque en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: si {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} fe como un grano de mostaza, {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}} a este monte: “Muévete de aquí hasta allá”, y se moverá, y nada será imposible para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».
es.B: Él les respondió: «Es porque {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} tan poca fe. En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que si {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} fe, aunque sea del tamaño de un grano de mostaza, {{plural_you:podrán|podréis}} decir a este monte: “Vete de aquí para allá”, y se irá. No habrá nada que no {{plural_you:puedan|podáis}} hacer».
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «Es porque {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} muy poca fe. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: supongamos que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe es tan pequeña como una diminuta semilla de mostaza. Aun así {{plural_you:podrán|podréis}} decirle a este monte: “Muévete de aquí para allá”, y se moverá. Nada será imposible para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « À cause de votre peu de foi. Car en vérité, je vous le dis, si vous avez de la foi comme un grain de moutarde, vous direz à cette montagne : “Passe d’ici à là-bas”, et elle passera, et rien ne vous sera impossible. »
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « C’est parce que votre foi est trop petite. En vérité, je vous le dis, si vous avez de la foi, même de la taille d’une graine de moutarde, vous pourrez dire à cette montagne : “Va d’ici jusque là-bas”, et elle ira. Rien ne vous sera impossible. »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « C’est parce que vous avez si peu de foi. Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : imaginez que votre foi soit seulement aussi grosse qu’une minuscule graine de moutarde. Même alors, vous pourrez dire à cette montagne : “Va d’ici jusque là-bas !”, et elle ira. Rien ne vous sera impossible. »

sw.L: Naye anawaambia, "Kwa sababu ya imani yenu ndogo. Kwa maana kweli nawaambia, mkiwa na imani kama punje ya haradali, mtauambia mlima huu, 'Hama kutoka hapa uende kule,' nao utahama; wala hakuna kitu kitakachowashinda."
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Ni kwa sababu imani yenu ni ndogo mno. Kweli nawaambia, kama mna imani hata iliyo ndogo kama mbegu ya haradali, mnaweza kuuambia mlima huu, 'Toka hapa uende pale,' nao utakwenda. Hakuna jambo ambalo hamtaweza kulifanya."
sw.R: Yesu aliwajibu, "Ni kwa sababu imani yenu ni ndogo sana. Nawaambia ukweli, tuseme imani yenu ni ndogo kama mbegu ndogo sana ya haradali. Hata hivyo mnaweza kuuambia mlima huu, 'Ondoka hapa uende pale,' nao utaondoka. Hakuna kitu kitakachowashinda."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Vì các con ít đức tin. Vì thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, nếu các con có đức tin như một hạt cải, các con sẽ nói với ngọn núi này: 'Hãy dời từ đây qua đó,' thì nó sẽ dời đi, và không có gì là không thể đối với các con."
vi.B: Ngài bảo họ: "Vì đức tin của các con quá ít. Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, nếu các con có đức tin chỉ nhỏ bằng hạt cải, các con có thể bảo ngọn núi này: 'Hãy dời từ đây qua đằng kia,' thì nó sẽ dời đi. Không có việc gì các con không làm được."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Vì đức tin của các con thật nhỏ bé. Ta nói thật với các con: giả sử đức tin của các con chỉ nhỏ như một hạt cải bé xíu thôi. Ngay cả như thế, các con cũng có thể nói với ngọn núi này: 'Hãy dời từ đây qua đằng kia,' và nó sẽ dời đi. Không có gì là không thể đối với các con."

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 말씀하신다. "너희의 작은 믿음 때문이다. 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 너희에게 겨자씨 한 알 같은 믿음이 있으면, 이 산에게 '여기에서 저기로 옮겨 가라' 하고 말할 것이다. 그러면 그것이 옮겨 갈 것이다. 그리고 너희에게 불가능한 것이 아무것도 없을 것이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희 믿음이 작기 때문이다. 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 너희에게 겨자씨 한 알만 한 믿음만 있어도, 이 산더러 '여기서 저기로 옮겨 가라' 하면 옮겨 갈 것이다. 너희가 하지 못할 일은 아무것도 없을 것이다."
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "너희 믿음이 너무 작기 때문이다. 내가 분명히 말한다. 너희 믿음이 아주 작은 겨자씨 한 알만큼밖에 안 된다고 해 보자. 그래도 너희가 이 산에게 '여기서 저기로 옮겨 가라' 하고 말하면, 산이 옮겨 갈 것이다. 너희가 할 수 없는 일은 하나도 없을 것이다."

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes diz: "Por causa da pouca fé de vocês. Pois em verdade eu lhes digo: se tiverem fé como um grão de mostarda, vocês dirão a este monte: 'Passa daqui para lá', e ele passará, e nada será impossível para vocês."
pt.B: Ele lhes respondeu: "É porque a fé de vocês é pequena demais. Em verdade eu lhes digo: se tiverem fé, mesmo do tamanho de uma semente de mostarda, vocês poderão dizer a este monte: 'Vai daqui para lá', e ele irá. Não haverá nada que vocês não possam fazer."
pt.R: Jesus respondeu: "É porque vocês têm muito pouca fé. Eu garanto a vocês: imaginem que a fé de vocês seja do tamanho de uma sementinha de mostarda. Mesmo assim, vocês poderão dizer a este monte: 'Sai daqui e vai para lá', e ele irá. Nada vai ser impossível para vocês."

decisions.choice: little faith, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: unbelief, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "unbelief", perhaps from "unbelieving" in 17:17. The SBLGNT reads "little faith", the word Jesus uses for the disciples in 6:30, 8:26 and 16:8. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: faith like a mustard seed: a very small faith that is real
decisions.reason: The mustard seed was the proverbial smallest seed (13:31-32). The point is not how much faith, but faith in God at all.

decisions.choice: move this mountain: do what seems impossible
alternatives: a promise to move actual mountains at will
decisions.reason: Moving mountains was a picture for overcoming what cannot be overcome (Zechariah 4:7; 1 Corinthians 13:2). Jesus says it again in 21:21.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verse 21
alternatives: verse 21, found in many later manuscripts: "But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting"
decisions.reason: Codex Sinaiticus (first hand), Codex Vaticanus and some early translations lack the verse. It is found in many later manuscripts and was probably added from Mark 9:29, where many manuscripts also add "and fasting". The verse number is skipped, so 17:22 follows 17:20. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

decisions.choice: says (L); told, answered (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: suppose your faith is only as big as a tiny mustard seed. Even then
alternatives: if you have faith like a grain of mustard
decisions.reason: Readable splits the condition into two short sentences and says that the seed was small.

decisions.choice: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo (L, B); {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The rendering of Jesus's single amen used through Matthew, recorded once in this passage. "De cierto" is the older form and now sounds dated.

decisions.choice: En vérité, je vous le dis (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R)
decisions.reason: The forms settled for the New Testament and used in Mark and Luke; Readable puts the solemn opening in an everyday sentence, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: un grain de moutarde (L); une graine de moutarde (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Luke 17:6: "grain" is the traditional and literal word for the seed (the Greek means a grain or kernel); "graine" is the everyday word for a seed one plants.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The rendering of Jesus's single amen used through Matthew, recorded once in this passage; John's double form is "Kweli kweli nawaambia".

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, Ta nói với các con" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các con" (R); "hạt cải"
decisions.reason: The settled forms for "Truly I tell you" and the mustard seed (13:31). Literal keeps Matthew's present "says" without "đã".

decisions.choice: "ít đức tin" (L), "đức tin ... quá ít" (B), "thật nhỏ bé" (R)
decisions.reason: The noun of the settled "người ít đức tin" (8:26; 16:8), with the key term "đức tin" at every level.

decisions.choice: "작은 믿음" (L), "믿음이 작다" (B, R); "진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B), "내가 분명히 말한다" (R); "겨자씨 한 알"; present "말씀하신다" (L)
decisions.reason: "Little faith" in the words of "믿음이 작은 사람들아" (16:8); the amen formula settled for the Korean Gospels; "겨자씨 한 알" as in the Korean Matthew 13:31. Literal keeps Matthew's present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: em verdade eu lhes digo (L, B); Eu garanto a vocês (R)
decisions.reason: The solemn opening in the words set for the New Testament (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 6). Readable says "Eu garanto a vocês", the plain Brazilian way of vouching for what follows.

decisions.choice: Passa (L); Vai (B); Sai ... e vai (R): the "tu" imperative
decisions.reason: A command to a mountain is not one person speaking to another, and Portuguese traditionally gives such commands in the "tu" form; "Vá daqui" would sound like brushing someone off.

source.text: Συστρεφομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μέλλει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: Gathering and they in the Galilee said to them the Jesus, Is about the Son of the Man to be handed over into hands of men, \v 23 and they will kill him, and on the third day he will be raised.

en.L: And as they were gathering in Galilee, Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man is about to be handed over into [the] hands of {{gender:human beings|men}}, \v 23 and they will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised."
en.B: As they were gathering in Galilee, Jesus told them, "The Son of Man is going to be given over into the power of human beings. \v 23 They will put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death, and on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised up."
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were gathering together in Galilee. Jesus said to them, "Soon the Son of Man will be handed over to the power of people. \v 23 They will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised from death."

es.L: Y mientras ellos se reunían en Galilea, Jesús les dijo: «El Hijo del Hombre está a punto de ser entregado en manos de {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}}, \v 23 y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} matarán, y al tercer día será resucitado».
es.B: Mientras se reunían en Galilea, Jesús les dijo: «El Hijo del Hombre va a ser entregado en poder de los seres humanos. \v 23 Lo matarán, y al tercer día será resucitado».
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos se estaban reuniendo en Galilea. Jesús les dijo: «Pronto el Hijo del Hombre será entregado en poder de la gente. \v 23 Lo matarán. Pero al tercer día será resucitado de la muerte».

fr.L: Et comme ils se rassemblaient en Galilée, Jésus leur dit : « Le Fils de l’homme va être livré entre les mains des {{gender:humains|hommes}}, \v 23 et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tueront, et le troisième jour {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera ressuscité. »
fr.B: Comme ils se trouvaient réunis en Galilée, Jésus leur dit : « Le Fils de l’homme va être livré au pouvoir des êtres humains. \v 23 Ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mettront à mort, et le troisième jour {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera ressuscité. »
fr.R: Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples se retrouvaient ensemble en Galilée. Jésus leur a dit : « Bientôt, le Fils de l’homme va être livré au pouvoir des gens. \v 23 Ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tueront. Mais le troisième jour, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera ramené de la mort à la vie. »

sw.L: Na wao walipokuwa wakikusanyika Galilaya, Yesu aliwaambia, "Mwana wa Adamu anakaribia kukabidhiwa mikononi mwa wanadamu, \v 23 nao watamuua, na siku ya tatu atafufuliwa."
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakikusanyika Galilaya, Yesu aliwaambia, "Mwana wa Adamu atatolewa katika mamlaka ya wanadamu. \v 23 Watamuua, na siku ya tatu atafufuliwa."
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wakikusanyika Galilaya. Yesu aliwaambia, "Karibuni Mwana wa Adamu atakabidhiwa katika mamlaka ya watu. \v 23 Watamuua. Lakini siku ya tatu atafufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu."

vi.L: Và khi họ đang tụ họp tại Ga-li-lê, Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Con Người sắp bị nộp vào tay người ta, \v 23 và họ sẽ giết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và đến ngày thứ ba {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ được sống lại."
vi.B: Khi họ đang tụ họp tại Ga-li-lê, Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Con Người sắp bị nộp vào tay loài người. \v 23 Họ sẽ giết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và đến ngày thứ ba {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ được sống lại."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ đang tụ họp tại miền Ga-li-lê. Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Chẳng bao lâu nữa, Con Người sẽ bị nộp vào quyền lực của người ta. \v 23 Họ sẽ giết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Nhưng đến ngày thứ ba, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ được sống lại từ cõi chết."

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 갈릴리에서 모여 있을 때에, 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "인자가 사람들의 손에 넘겨지게 되어 있다. \v 23 그리고 그들이 그를 죽일 것이다. 그리고 셋째 날에 그가 살아날 것이다."
ko.B: 그들이 갈릴리에 모여 있을 때에, 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "인자가 곧 사람들의 손에 넘겨질 것이다. \v 23 그들이 그를 죽일 것이다. 그러나 그는 셋째 날에 다시 살아날 것이다."
ko.R: 예수와 제자들이 갈릴리에 함께 모였다. 그때 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "이제 곧 인자가 사람들에게 넘겨질 것이다. \v 23 그들이 인자를 죽일 것이다. 그러나 셋째 날에 하나님께서 인자를 다시 살리실 것이다."

pt.L: E, enquanto eles se reuniam na Galileia, Jesus lhes disse: "O Filho do Homem está para ser entregue nas mãos {{gender:dos seres humanos|dos homens}}, \v 23 e eles {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} matarão, e no terceiro dia {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} será ressuscitado."
pt.B: Enquanto se reuniam na Galileia, Jesus lhes disse: "O Filho do Homem vai ser entregue ao poder dos seres humanos. \v 23 Eles {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} matarão, e no terceiro dia {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} será ressuscitado."
pt.R: Jesus e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores estavam se reunindo na Galileia. Jesus disse a eles: "Logo o Filho do Homem vai ser entregue ao poder das pessoas. \v 23 Elas vão matá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}. Mas no terceiro dia {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} vai ser ressuscitado dos mortos."

decisions.choice: the second time Jesus tells of his death and raising
decisions.reason: Jesus first said this in 16:21 and says it again in 20:18-19. Here he adds that he will be handed over.

decisions.choice: handed over: given up into others' power, by Judas and in God's plan
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Judas giving Jesus up (26:15-16). The passive leaves the actor unnamed and may also point to God's purpose.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man into the hands of men: a play on words
decisions.reason: The one called the Son of Man is handed over to human beings. The repeated word makes the contrast sharp.

decisions.choice: as they were gathering, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: as they were staying, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have a verb meaning "while they were staying" in Galilee. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: into the power of human beings (B); to the power of people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "into the hands of" means. Literal keeps the wordplay, with the gender setting on "men".

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers
decisions.reason: Readable says who was gathering.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre ... {{gender:seres humanos|hombres}} (L); los seres humanos (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek plays on "the Son of Man" and "men" (meaning decision m3). "Seres humanos" keeps the link with "Hombre" in the sense of humankind, and the traditional "hombres" of the setting keeps the very word. "El Hijo del Hombre" is the title used through Matthew, never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: "des {{gender:humains|hommes}}" (L); "des êtres humains" (B) and "des gens" (R) with no setting
decisions.reason: As Mark 9:31 and Luke 9:44: the noun is the general word for human beings, so Literal takes the inclusive default with "hommes" as the alternative, which keeps the play with "Fils de l’homme" (m3). "Êtres humains" and "gens" already include everyone.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu ... wanadamu
decisions.reason: The Greek plays on "the Son of Man" and "men" (meaning decision m3). "Wanadamu" (human beings) echoes "Adamu" in the title, so Literal and Balanced keep the play. "Mwana wa Adamu" is the title used through Matthew, never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: "bị nộp" at every level; "người ta", "loài người" with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in Mark 9:31: the same verb for "handed over" through the predictions. "Con Người ... tay loài người" keeps something of the play on words (meaning decision); the Vietnamese words take in men and women.

decisions.choice: "인자" ... "사람들의 손"; "넘겨지다" at every level; "사람들" with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 9:31. Korean "인자" and "사람들" keep the play on "Son of Man" and "men" (meaning decision) only faintly; "사람" already includes men and women, so the English gender span has nothing to change. Jesus speaks of the Son of Man without honorifics.

decisions.choice: "하나님께서 인자를 다시 살리실 것이다" (R)
decisions.reason: The passive "will be raised" means raised by God, as in 16:21; Readable names God, as the Korean Matthew 16:21 does.

en.B: And the disciples were filled with deep sorrow.

es.B: Y los discípulos se llenaron de profunda tristeza.
es.R: Los discípulos se pusieron muy tristes.

fr.B: Et les disciples furent remplis d’une profonde tristesse.
fr.R: Les disciples sont devenus très tristes.

vi.L: Và họ vô cùng buồn rầu.
vi.B: Các môn đồ vô cùng buồn rầu.

pt.B: E os discípulos ficaram profundamente tristes.

decisions.choice: they were exceedingly grieved: they grasped that he would die
decisions.reason: Their grief shows they heard that Jesus would be killed. Matthew does not say whether they understood that he would be raised.

decisions.choice: the disciples (B); the followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who grieved.

source.text: Ἐλθόντων δὲ αὐτῶν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ προσῆλθον οἱ τὰ δίδραχμα λαμβάνοντες τῷ Πέτρῳ καὶ εἶπαν· Ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν οὐ τελεῖ τὰ δίδραχμα;

records.literal_gloss: Having come and they to Capernaum came those the two-drachmas collecting to the Peter and said, The teacher of you not pays the two-drachmas?

en.L: And when they came to Capernaum, those who collected the two drachmas came to Peter and said, "Does your teacher not pay the two drachmas?"
en.B: When they arrived in Capernaum, the men who collected the {{units:temple tax|two-drachma tax}} came to Peter and said, "Your teacher pays the {{units:temple tax|two-drachma tax}}, does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not?"
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers went to the town of Capernaum. There the men who collected the {{units:temple tax|two-drachma tax}} came to Peter. They asked him, "Your teacher pays the {{units:temple tax|two-drachma tax}}, does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not?"

es.L: Y cuando llegaron a Cafarnaúm, se acercaron a Pedro los que cobraban las dos dracmas y dijeron: «¿El maestro {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}} no paga las dos dracmas?».
es.B: Cuando llegaron a Cafarnaúm, los que cobraban {{units:el impuesto del templo|el impuesto de las dos dracmas}} se acercaron a Pedro y le dijeron: «El maestro {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}} paga {{units:el impuesto del templo|el impuesto de las dos dracmas}}, ¿verdad?».
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos fueron al pueblo de Cafarnaúm. Allí, los hombres que cobraban {{units:el impuesto del templo|el impuesto de las dos dracmas}} se acercaron a Pedro. Le preguntaron: «El maestro {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}} paga {{units:el impuesto del templo|el impuesto de las dos dracmas}}, ¿no es así?».

fr.L: Et quand ils furent arrivés à Capharnaüm, ceux qui percevaient les deux drachmes s’approchèrent de Pierre et dirent : « Votre maître ne paie-t-il pas les deux drachmes ? »
fr.B: Quand ils arrivèrent à Capharnaüm, les hommes qui percevaient {{units:la taxe du temple|la taxe des deux drachmes}} vinrent trouver Pierre et lui dirent : « Votre maître paie bien {{units:la taxe du temple|la taxe des deux drachmes}}, n’est-ce pas ? »
fr.R: Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples sont allés dans la ville de Capharnaüm. Là, les hommes qui faisaient payer {{units:la taxe du temple|la taxe des deux drachmes}} sont venus voir Pierre. Ils lui ont demandé : « Votre maître paie bien {{units:la taxe du temple|la taxe des deux drachmes}}, n’est-ce pas ? »

sw.L: Na walipofika Kapernaumu, wale waliokuwa wakikusanya drakma mbili walimjia Petro, wakasema, "Je, mwalimu wenu halipi drakma mbili?"
sw.B: Walipofika Kapernaumu, watu waliokuwa wakikusanya {{units:kodi ya hekalu|kodi ya drakma mbili}} walimjia Petro, wakamwuliza, "Mwalimu wenu hulipa {{units:kodi ya hekalu|kodi ya drakma mbili}}, sivyo?"
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikwenda katika mji wa Kapernaumu. Huko watu waliokuwa wakikusanya {{units:kodi ya hekalu|kodi ya drakma mbili}} walimjia Petro. Wakamwuliza, "Mwalimu wenu hulipa {{units:kodi ya hekalu|kodi ya drakma mbili}}, sivyo?"

vi.L: Và khi họ đến Ca-bê-na-um, những người thu [thuế] hai đơ-rắc-ma đến gặp Phi-e-rơ và nói: "Thầy của các anh không nộp [thuế] hai đơ-rắc-ma sao?"
vi.B: Khi họ đến Ca-bê-na-um, những người thu {{units:thuế đền thờ|thuế hai đơ-rắc-ma}} đến gặp Phi-e-rơ và hỏi: "Thầy của các anh vẫn nộp {{units:thuế đền thờ|thuế hai đơ-rắc-ma}}, phải không?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ đến thị trấn Ca-bê-na-um. Ở đó, những người thu {{units:thuế đền thờ|thuế hai đơ-rắc-ma}} đến gặp Phi-e-rơ. Họ hỏi ông: "Thầy của các anh có nộp {{units:thuế đền thờ|thuế hai đơ-rắc-ma}} chứ?"

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 가버나움에 이르렀을 때, 두 드라크마를 거두는 사람들이 베드로에게 와서 말했다. "여러분의 선생님은 두 드라크마를 내지 않으십니까?"
ko.B: 그들이 가버나움에 이르렀을 때, {{units:성전세|두 드라크마}}를 거두는 사람들이 베드로에게 와서 물었다. "여러분의 선생님은 {{units:성전세|두 드라크마}}를 내시지요?"
ko.R: 예수와 제자들이 가버나움 마을에 갔다. 거기서 {{units:성전세|두 드라크마}}를 거두는 사람들이 베드로에게 와서 물었다. "여러분의 선생님은 {{units:성전세|두 드라크마}}를 내시지요?"

pt.L: E, quando chegaram a Cafarnaum, os que cobravam as duas dracmas se aproximaram de Pedro e disseram: "O mestre de vocês não paga as duas dracmas?"
pt.B: Quando chegaram a Cafarnaum, os homens que cobravam o {{units:imposto do templo|imposto das duas dracmas}} foram até Pedro e perguntaram: "O mestre de vocês paga o {{units:imposto do templo|imposto das duas dracmas}}, não paga?"
pt.R: Jesus e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores foram à cidade de Cafarnaum. Lá, os homens que cobravam o {{units:imposto do templo|imposto das duas dracmas}} foram até Pedro. Eles perguntaram a Pedro: "O mestre de vocês paga o {{units:imposto do templo|imposto das duas dracmas}}, não paga?"

decisions.choice: the two drachmas: the half-shekel tax for the temple
decisions.reason: Every Jewish man aged twenty and over paid half a shekel each year for the service of the temple (Exodus 30:11-16; Nehemiah 10:32). In Jesus's day it was paid as two drachmas, about two days' wages. It was a tax of the Jewish people for God's house, not a tax of Rome.

decisions.choice: does he not pay: a question that expects yes
decisions.reason: The form of the question expects the answer "yes", and Peter gives it (17:25).

decisions.choice: Capernaum: the town where Jesus lived
alternatives: a town he was passing through
decisions.reason: Jesus had made his home in Capernaum (4:13; 9:1).

decisions.choice: temple tax (default); two-drachma tax (alternative)
decisions.reason: The Measures setting gives the original name of the tax. Literal keeps the original "two drachmas".

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers; the town of
decisions.reason: Readable says who came, and that Capernaum was a town.

decisions.choice: el maestro {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}}
decisions.reason: "Your" is plural: the collectors speak to Peter as one of Jesus's company. With ustedes, "su maestro" could be read as "his teacher", so the text says "de ustedes".

decisions.choice: {{units:el impuesto del templo|el impuesto de las dos dracmas}}
decisions.reason: As in the English, the default names what the coins paid for, the half-shekel tax for the temple (meaning decision m1), and the alternative keeps the coins. Literal keeps "las dos dracmas".

decisions.choice: votre maître
decisions.reason: French calls a respected teacher "maître", as Mark uses "Maître" in address; "enseignant" names a school job. The context of a teacher and his disciples shows that an owner is not meant.

decisions.choice: {{units:kodi ya hekalu|kodi ya drakma mbili}}
decisions.reason: As in the English, the default names what the coins paid for, the half-shekel tax for the temple (meaning decision m1), and the alternative keeps the coins. Literal keeps "drakma mbili".

decisions.choice: {{units:thuế đền thờ|thuế hai đơ-rắc-ma}} (B, R); "[thuế] hai đơ-rắc-ma" (L)
decisions.reason: As in the English: the default names what the tax was, the half-shekel for the temple (meaning decision), and the alternative keeps the coin. "Đơ-rắc-ma" transliterates the Greek coin's name.

decisions.choice: "Thầy của các anh" in the collectors' words, with no deity_pronoun span; "các anh" for Peter and the disciples
decisions.reason: The collectors speak of Jesus as the disciples' teacher, a noun that takes no setting span; they are not his opponents, so they speak politely. The Greek "your" is singular; Vietnamese uses the plural "các anh" since Jesus is the teacher of all the disciples.

decisions.choice: "{{units:성전세|두 드라크마}}" (B, R); "두 드라크마" (L)
decisions.reason: The two drachmas were the yearly half-shekel tax for the temple (meaning decision, with footnote). As in the English, the default says what the tax was and the alternative keeps the coin; the Korean particle "를" fits both forms, which both end in a vowel.

decisions.choice: The collectors speak to Peter in polite 합쇼체/해요체 and honour Jesus as "여러분의 선생님" with "-시-"
decisions.reason: They are officials asking a routine question, not open opponents, so they speak courteously of a known teacher; the question expecting yes (meaning decision) is "내시지요?" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: paga ..., não paga?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes" (m2). Portuguese marks that with the tag "não paga?", repeating the verb, the way Brazilians ask for agreement; Literal keeps the Greek's negative question.

fr.R: Pierre a répondu : « Oui, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la paie. »

decisions.choice: Yes: Peter answers for Jesus without asking him
decisions.reason: Peter assumes that Jesus pays the tax. Jesus takes up the question in the house (17:25-27).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: Peter; he does
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Peter and complete his short answer.

decisions.choice: Present "말한다" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Matthew's present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: Sim, paga
decisions.reason: Portuguese answers a yes-question by repeating the verb, with no subject pronoun, so the English span on "he does" has no counterpart.

source.text: καὶ ἐλθόντα εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προέφθασεν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Τί σοι δοκεῖ, Σίμων;

records.literal_gloss: And having come into the house anticipated him the Jesus saying, What to you seems, Simon?

en.L: And when he came into the house, Jesus spoke to him first, saying, "What do you think, Simon?
en.B: When Peter came into the house, Jesus spoke to him before he could say anything. "Simon," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "tell me what you think.
en.R: Peter went into the house. Before he could say anything, Jesus spoke to him. Jesus said, "Simon, what do you think?

es.L: Y cuando él entró en la casa, Jesús se le anticipó, diciendo: «¿Qué te parece, Simón?
es.B: Cuando Pedro entró en la casa, Jesús le habló antes de que él dijera nada: «Dime, Simón, ¿qué piensas?
es.R: Pedro entró en la casa. Antes de que pudiera decir algo, Jesús le habló. Le dijo: «Simón, ¿qué piensas?

fr.L: Et quand il fut entré dans la maison, Jésus le devança, disant : « Que te semble-t-il, Simon ?
fr.B: Quand Pierre entra dans la maison, Jésus prit la parole avant qu’il ait pu dire un mot. « Simon, dit-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, dis-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ce que tu penses.
fr.R: Pierre est entré dans la maison. Avant qu’il ait pu dire quoi que ce soit, Jésus lui a parlé. Il lui a dit : « Simon, qu’est-ce que tu en penses ?

sw.L: Na alipoingia ndani ya nyumba, Yesu akamwahi, akisema, "Unafikiri nini, Simoni?
sw.B: Petro alipoingia nyumbani, Yesu alimwahi kabla hajasema neno. Akasema, "Simoni, niambie unavyofikiri.
sw.R: Petro aliingia ndani ya nyumba. Kabla hajasema chochote, Yesu alianza kuongea naye. Yesu akasema, "Simoni, unafikiri nini?

vi.L: Và khi ông vào nhà, Đức Giê-xu nói trước với ông rằng: "Si-môn, con nghĩ thế nào?
vi.B: Khi Phi-e-rơ vào nhà, Đức Giê-xu nói với ông trước khi ông kịp nói gì: "Si-môn, hãy cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết con nghĩ sao.
vi.R: Phi-e-rơ đi vào nhà. Trước khi ông kịp nói gì, Đức Giê-xu đã nói với ông: "Si-môn, con nghĩ sao?

ko.L: 그리고 그가 집에 들어갔을 때, 예수께서 먼저 그에게 말씀하셨다. "시몬아, 너는 어떻게 생각하느냐?
ko.B: 베드로가 집에 들어가자, 그가 말을 꺼내기도 전에 예수께서 먼저 말씀하셨다. "시몬아, 네 생각은 어떠냐?
ko.R: 베드로가 집 안으로 들어갔다. 베드로가 무슨 말을 하기도 전에 예수께서 먼저 말씀하셨다. "시몬아, 너는 어떻게 생각하느냐?

pt.L: E, quando ele entrou na casa, Jesus se antecipou a ele, dizendo: "O que você acha, Simão?
pt.B: Quando Pedro entrou na casa, Jesus falou com ele antes que ele dissesse alguma coisa. "Simão", disse {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, "diga-me o que você acha.
pt.R: Pedro entrou na casa. Antes que ele dissesse alguma coisa, Jesus falou com ele. Jesus disse: "Simão, o que você acha?

decisions.choice: spoke to him first: before Peter could raise the matter
decisions.reason: The verb means to come before or anticipate. Jesus raises the question before Peter tells him of it, which suggests he already knew.

decisions.choice: the house: probably the house in Capernaum where Jesus stayed
decisions.reason: Peter had a house in Capernaum (8:14), and Jesus is often in "the house" there (9:28; 13:1, 36).

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who came into the house.

decisions.choice: "con" for Simon
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to his disciple as "con", as in 16:17-19.

source.text: οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τίνων λαμβάνουσιν τέλη ἢ κῆνσον;

records.literal_gloss: The kings of the earth from whom take tolls or tax?

en.L: The kings of the earth, from whom do they take tolls or tax?
en.B: When the kings of the earth take tolls or taxes, who pays them?
en.R: The kings of this world collect taxes and fees. Who do they collect them from?

es.L: Los reyes de la tierra, ¿de quiénes reciben aranceles o tributo?
es.B: Cuando los reyes de la tierra cobran aranceles o impuestos, ¿quién los paga?
es.R: Los reyes de este mundo cobran impuestos y tasas. ¿A quién se los cobran?

fr.L: Les rois de la terre, de qui perçoivent-ils des droits ou un impôt ?
fr.B: Quand les rois de la terre perçoivent des droits ou des impôts, qui les paie ?
fr.R: Les rois de ce monde font payer des impôts et des taxes. À qui est-ce qu’ils les font payer ?

sw.L: Wafalme wa dunia, huchukua ushuru au kodi ya kichwa kutoka kwa nani?
sw.B: Wafalme wa dunia wanapotoza ushuru au kodi, ni nani anayelipa?
sw.R: Wafalme wa ulimwengu huu hukusanya kodi na ada. Huzikusanya kutoka kwa nani?

vi.L: Các vua trên đất thu thuế quan hay thuế thân từ ai?
vi.B: Khi các vua trên đất thu thuế hàng hóa hay thuế thân, thì ai phải nộp?
vi.R: Các vua trên thế gian thu thuế và lệ phí. Họ thu từ ai?

ko.L: 땅의 왕들은 누구에게서 관세나 세금을 받느냐?
ko.B: 세상 왕들이 관세나 세금을 받을 때, 누구에게서 받느냐?
ko.R: 세상의 왕들은 세금과 통행료를 거둔다. 그들은 누구에게서 그것을 거두느냐?

pt.L: Os reis da terra, de quem cobram tributos ou imposto?
pt.B: Quando os reis da terra cobram tributos ou impostos, quem paga?
pt.R: Os reis deste mundo cobram impostos e taxas. De quem eles cobram?

decisions.choice: tolls or tax: duties on goods and a tax on each person
decisions.reason: The first word means duties such as tolls on goods. The second, borrowed from Latin, is the tax paid by each person, the tax of 22:17-19.

decisions.choice: the kings of the earth: human rulers
decisions.reason: The phrase means rulers of this world, set against God as king (Psalm 2:2). The comparison leads to God and his house.

decisions.choice: a statement, then the question
decisions.reason: Readable states the fact and then asks the question.

decisions.choice: ushuru au kodi ya kichwa
decisions.reason: The two Greek words are duties on goods and a tax on each person (meaning decision m1). "Kodi ya kichwa" (head tax) shows the second at Literal; Balanced and Readable use the general words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "thuế quan hay thuế thân" (L); "thuế hàng hóa hay thuế thân" (B)
decisions.reason: Duties on goods and a tax on each person (meaning decision); "thuế thân" is the Vietnamese word for a poll tax.

decisions.choice: "땅의 왕들" (L), "세상 왕들" (B, R); "관세", "세금"
decisions.reason: The kings of the earth are human rulers (meaning decision); the two words are duties on goods and a tax on each person.

source.text: ἀπὸ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῶν ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων;

records.literal_gloss: From the sons of them or from the strangers?

en.L: From their sons, or from strangers?"
en.B: From their own sons, or from people outside their family?"
en.R: Do they collect from their own sons, or from other people?"

es.L: ¿De sus hijos o de los extraños?».
es.B: ¿De sus propios hijos o de los que no son de su familia?».
es.R: ¿Se los cobran a sus propios hijos o a otras personas?».

fr.L: De leurs fils, ou des étrangers ? »
fr.B: Leurs propres fils, ou des gens étrangers à leur famille ? »
fr.R: Est-ce qu’ils les font payer à leurs propres fils, ou à d’autres gens ? »

sw.L: Kutoka kwa wana wao au kutoka kwa wageni?"
sw.B: Kwa wana wao wenyewe, au kwa watu wasio wa familia yao?"
sw.R: Je, huzikusanya kutoka kwa wana wao wenyewe, au kutoka kwa watu wengine?"

vi.L: Từ con cái của họ hay từ người ngoài?"
vi.B: Từ chính con cái của họ, hay từ những người ngoài gia đình?"
vi.R: Họ thu từ chính con cái mình, hay từ người khác?"

ko.B: 자기 아들들에게서냐, 아니면 집안사람이 아닌 남들에게서냐?"
ko.R: 자기 아들들에게서 거두느냐, 아니면 다른 사람들에게서 거두느냐?"

pt.L: Dos filhos deles ou dos estranhos?"
pt.B: Dos próprios filhos ou de gente de fora da família?"
pt.R: Eles cobram dos próprios filhos ou das outras pessoas?"

decisions.choice: strangers: people not of the king's family
decisions.reason: The word means those who belong to others. Here it is everyone outside the royal household, the king's subjects.

decisions.choice: sons, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The picture is of a king's household, and it leads to Jesus, God's Son (17:5, 26). The word is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: people outside their family
decisions.reason: Balanced says who the strangers are in this picture.

decisions.choice: "con cái" for "sons", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English keeps "sons" with no setting; Vietnamese "con cái" means the king's children, the family set against outsiders, which is the point (meaning decision), and "con trai" would narrow it needlessly. The picture still points to the Son in 17:26.

decisions.choice: "아들들" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The king's sons stand in the picture for the Son (meaning decision on 17:26), so, as in the English, there is no gender span here.

source.text: εἰπόντος δέ· Ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων, ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἄρα γε ἐλεύθεροί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοί.

records.literal_gloss: Having said and, From the strangers, said to him the Jesus, Then indeed free are the sons.

en.L: And when he said, "From strangers," Jesus said to him, "Then the sons are free.
en.B: "From outsiders," Peter replied. Jesus said to him, "So the sons owe nothing.
en.R: Peter answered, "From other people." Jesus said to him, "Then the sons do not have to pay.

es.L: Y cuando él dijo: «De los extraños», Jesús le dijo: «Por tanto, los hijos están libres.
es.B: «De los de fuera», respondió Pedro. Jesús le dijo: «Entonces los hijos no deben nada.
es.R: Pedro respondió: «De otras personas». Jesús le dijo: «Entonces los hijos no tienen que pagar.

fr.L: Et comme il disait : « Des étrangers », Jésus lui déclara : « Les fils sont donc libres.
fr.B: « Les étrangers », répondit Pierre. Jésus lui dit : « Les fils ne doivent donc rien.
fr.R: Pierre a répondu : « Les autres gens. » Jésus lui a dit : « Alors les fils n’ont pas à payer.

sw.L: Naye aliposema, "Kutoka kwa wageni," Yesu akamwambia, "Basi wana wako huru.
sw.B: Petro alijibu, "Kutoka kwa watu wa nje." Yesu akamwambia, "Basi wana hawadaiwi kitu.
sw.R: Petro alijibu, "Kutoka kwa watu wengine." Yesu akamwambia, "Basi wana hawalazimiki kulipa.

vi.L: Và khi ông nói: "Từ người ngoài," Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Vậy thì con cái được miễn.
vi.B: Phi-e-rơ thưa: "Từ người ngoài." Đức Giê-xu bảo ông: "Vậy thì con cái không phải nộp gì cả.
vi.R: Phi-e-rơ trả lời: "Từ người khác." Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Vậy thì con cái không phải nộp thuế.

ko.L: 그가 "남들에게서입니다" 하고 말하자, 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "그렇다면 아들들은 자유롭다.
ko.B: 베드로가 "남들에게서 받습니다" 하고 대답하자, 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "그렇다면 아들들은 낼 의무가 없다.
ko.R: 베드로가 대답했다. "다른 사람들에게서 거둡니다." 그러자 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "그렇다면 아들들은 낼 필요가 없다.

pt.L: E, quando ele disse: "Dos estranhos", Jesus lhe disse: "Então os filhos são livres.
pt.B: "Dos de fora", respondeu Pedro. Jesus lhe disse: "Então os filhos não devem nada.
pt.R: Pedro respondeu: "Das outras pessoas." Jesus disse a ele: "Então os filhos não precisam pagar.

decisions.choice: the sons are free: God's Son owes no tax for his Father's house
alternatives: a statement about earthly kings only
a ruling that no Jew need pay the temple tax
decisions.reason: The temple tax was paid to God, the great king. Jesus is God's Son (17:5), so he owes nothing. The plural "sons" may include his disciples as God's children, since the coin pays for Peter too (17:27).

decisions.choice: then indeed: the conclusion follows from Peter's answer
decisions.reason: The words draw the conclusion Peter's own answer requires.

decisions.choice: owe nothing (B); do not have to pay (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "free" means in a talk about taxes.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

decisions.choice: "자유롭다" (L); "낼 의무가 없다" (B); "낼 필요가 없다" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word "free", which carries the meaning decision's point that God's Son owes no tax for his Father's house; Balanced and Readable say what the freedom is here.

source.text: ἵνα δὲ μὴ σκανδαλίσωμεν αὐτούς, πορευθεὶς εἰς θάλασσαν βάλε ἄγκιστρον καὶ τὸν ἀναβάντα πρῶτον ἰχθὺν ἆρον, καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εὑρήσεις στατῆρα· ἐκεῖνον λαβὼν δὸς αὐτοῖς ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ καὶ σοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: So that but not we may offend them, having gone to sea cast a hook and the having come up first fish take, and having opened the mouth of it you will find a stater; that having taken give to them for me and you.

en.L: But so that we do not offend them, go to [the] sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up, and when you open its mouth you will find a stater. Take that and give [it] to them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you."
en.B: Still, we do not want to give them a reason to take offense. So go down to the lake and throw in a hook. Take the first fish that comes up, open its mouth, and you will find {{units:a silver coin worth four days' wages|a stater}}. Take it and give it to them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and for you."
en.R: But we do not want to upset these men. So go to the lake and throw in a fishing line with a hook. Pull in the first fish you catch. Open its mouth, and you will find {{units:a silver coin worth four days' pay|a stater}}. That is enough to pay the tax for two people. Take it and give it to them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and for you."

es.L: Pero, para que no los escandalicemos, ve al mar, lanza un anzuelo y saca el primer pez que suba; y abriéndole la boca encontrarás un estatero. Toma esa [moneda] y dásela a ellos por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y por ti».
es.B: Sin embargo, no queremos darles motivo de ofensa. Así que ve al lago y echa un anzuelo. Saca el primer pez que pique, ábrele la boca y encontrarás {{units:una moneda de plata que vale cuatro días de salario|un estatero}}. Toma esa moneda y dásela a ellos por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y por ti».
es.R: Pero no queremos molestar a estos hombres. Así que ve al lago y echa un sedal con anzuelo. Saca el primer pez que pesques. Ábrele la boca y encontrarás {{units:una moneda de plata que vale lo que se gana en cuatro días|un estatero}}. Eso alcanza para pagar el impuesto de dos personas. Toma esa moneda y dásela a ellos por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y por ti».

fr.L: Mais pour que nous ne les scandalisions pas, va à la mer, jette un hameçon, et prends le premier poisson qui montera ; et, en lui ouvrant la bouche, tu trouveras un statère. Prends-le et donne-le-leur pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et pour toi. »
fr.B: Pourtant, nous ne voulons pas leur donner une raison d’être choqués. Va donc au lac et jette un hameçon. Prends le premier poisson qui mordra, ouvre-lui la bouche, et tu y trouveras {{units:une pièce d’argent valant quatre journées de salaire|un statère}}. Remets-leur cette somme pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et pour toi. »
fr.R: Mais nous ne voulons pas fâcher ces hommes. Alors va au lac et lance une ligne avec un hameçon. Tire hors de l’eau le premier poisson que tu attraperas. Ouvre-lui la bouche : tu y trouveras {{units:une pièce d’argent qui vaut quatre jours de salaire|un statère}}. Cela suffit pour payer la taxe de deux personnes. Va leur donner cet argent pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et pour toi. »

sw.L: Lakini ili tusiwakwaze, nenda baharini, utupe ndoano, umvue samaki wa kwanza atakayepanda, na ukimfungua mdomo utakuta stateri; ichukue hiyo, uwape badala {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na yako."
sw.B: Hata hivyo, hatutaki kuwapa sababu ya kuchukizwa. Kwa hiyo nenda ziwani, utupe ndoano. Mvue samaki wa kwanza atakayenaswa, umfungue mdomo, nawe utakuta {{units:sarafu ya fedha yenye thamani ya mshahara wa siku nne|stateri}}. Ichukue, uwape kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kwa ajili yako."
sw.R: Lakini hatutaki kuwaudhi watu hawa. Kwa hiyo nenda ziwani, utupe mshipi wenye ndoano. Mvute samaki wa kwanza utakayemvua. Fungua mdomo wake, nawe utakuta {{units:sarafu ya fedha yenye thamani ya mshahara wa siku nne|stateri}}. Inatosha kulipa kodi ya watu wawili. Ichukue, uwape kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kwa ajili yako."

vi.L: Nhưng để chúng ta khỏi làm cho họ vấp phạm, hãy ra biển, thả lưỡi câu, và bắt con cá nào cắn câu trước, mở miệng nó ra, con sẽ thấy một đồng sta-te. Hãy lấy đồng ấy và đưa cho họ thay cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và con."
vi.B: Tuy vậy, chúng ta không muốn làm cho họ vấp phạm. Vậy con hãy ra hồ thả câu. Con cá nào cắn câu trước, con hãy bắt lấy, mở miệng nó ra, con sẽ thấy {{units:một đồng bạc trị giá bốn ngày công|một đồng sta-te}}. Hãy lấy đồng ấy và đưa cho họ để nộp thuế cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và cho con."
vi.R: Nhưng chúng ta không muốn làm cho những người này bực mình. Vậy con hãy ra hồ thả cần câu có lưỡi câu xuống nước. Hãy kéo con cá đầu tiên con câu được lên. Mở miệng nó ra, con sẽ thấy {{units:một đồng bạc trị giá bốn ngày công|một đồng sta-te}}. Số tiền ấy đủ để nộp thuế cho hai người. Hãy lấy đồng ấy và đưa cho họ để nộp thuế cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và cho con."

ko.L: 그러나 우리가 그들을 걸려 넘어지게 하지 않도록, 바다로 가서 낚시를 던져라. 그리고 처음 올라오는 물고기를 잡아라. 그 입을 열면 스타테르 한 닢을 찾을 것이다. 그것을 가져다가 나와 너를 대신하여 그들에게 주어라."
ko.B: 그러나 우리가 그들의 비위를 거스를 까닭은 없다. 그러니 바다로 가서 낚시를 던져라. 처음 올라오는 물고기를 잡아 그 입을 열어 보면, {{units:나흘 품삯이 되는 은돈 한 닢|스타테르 한 닢}}을 찾을 것이다. 그것을 가져다가 나와 너의 몫으로 그들에게 주어라."
ko.R: 하지만 우리는 저 사람들의 마음을 상하게 하고 싶지 않다. 그러니 호수에 가서 낚싯줄을 던져라. 처음 잡히는 물고기를 끌어올려라. 그 입을 열어 보면 {{units:나흘 품삯이 되는 은돈 한 닢|스타테르 한 닢}}이 있을 것이다. 그것이면 두 사람의 세금을 낼 수 있다. 그것을 가져다가 나와 너의 세금으로 그들에게 주어라."

pt.L: Mas, para que não os escandalizemos, vá ao mar, jogue um anzol e pegue o primeiro peixe que subir; e, abrindo a boca dele, você encontrará um estáter. Pegue-o e dê a eles por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e por você."
pt.B: Mesmo assim, não queremos que eles tenham motivo para se ofender. Por isso, vá até o lago e jogue um anzol. Pegue o primeiro peixe que fisgar, abra a boca dele, e você vai encontrar {{units:uma moeda de prata que vale quatro dias de salário|um estáter}}. Pegue a moeda e entregue a eles por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e por você."
pt.R: Mas nós não queremos aborrecer esses homens. Então vá até o lago e jogue uma linha com anzol. Puxe o primeiro peixe que você pegar. Abra a boca dele, e você vai encontrar {{units:uma moeda de prata que vale quatro dias de pagamento|um estáter}}. Ela dá para pagar o imposto de duas pessoas. Pegue a moeda e entregue a eles por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e por você."

decisions.choice: offend them: give them cause to take offense
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause to stumble. Here it means giving the collectors and others a reason to think Jesus despised God's house.

decisions.choice: a stater: a silver coin worth four drachmas
decisions.reason: Four drachmas was about four days' wages, the tax for two men (17:24). One coin pays for Jesus and Peter together.

decisions.choice: for me and you: in payment for both
alternatives: in place of me but not of you
decisions.reason: The word means "in place of" or "in exchange for". The coin covers what each of them owed.

decisions.choice: the sea: the Sea of Galilee, beside Capernaum
decisions.reason: Capernaum lay on the shore of the lake. Matthew does not tell of Peter catching the fish; the story ends with Jesus's word.

decisions.choice: a silver coin worth four days' wages (B); a silver coin worth four days' pay (R); a stater (alternative)
decisions.reason: The Measures setting gives the original coin. Literal keeps "stater".

decisions.choice: the lake
decisions.reason: The Sea of Galilee is a lake, and Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: That is enough to pay the tax for two people.
decisions.reason: Readable says why one coin is enough for both.

decisions.choice: these men
decisions.reason: Readable says who might be upset: the men who collect the tax.

decisions.choice: el mar (L); el lago (B, R)
decisions.reason: The "sea" is the Sea of Galilee, beside Capernaum (meaning decision m4), a freshwater lake. Literal keeps the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say "lago", as the English does.

decisions.choice: {{units:una moneda de plata que vale cuatro días de salario|un estatero}}

decisions.reason: A stater was a silver coin worth four drachmas (meaning decision), about four days' wages; the default says its worth, the alternative keeps the coin, as in the English. The particles that follow ("을" in B, "이" in R) fit both forms.
